ver: Artifact-level version counter. Incremented on every write.
meta.title: Application name, copied from PRD meta.title.
meta.updated_at: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last write.
entities: List of all domain entities in the project. Each entity represents a core data concept. Do not include infrastructure or join-table concepts unless they have independent business meaning.
entities[].id: Kebab-case identifier for this entity, e.g. 'user', 'order', 'product-variant'. Stable across rewrites — used as a reference key in per-screen tech specs.
entities[].name: Human-readable name, e.g. 'User', 'Order', 'Product Variant'.
entities[].description: One sentence describing what this entity represents in the business domain.
entities[].fields: List of fields on this entity. Use types appropriate for the project's tech stack (from arch-spec). Common types: string, integer, float, boolean, uuid, timestamp, date, enum([values]), json.
entities[].fields[].name: Field name — use the naming convention from shared-decisions (e.g. snake_case).
entities[].fields[].type: Data type. Match the tech stack's type system. For enums, list values: e.g. 'enum(pending, active, cancelled)'.
entities[].fields[].required: true if this field must always have a value; false if nullable/optional.
entities[].fields[].description: What this field stores and any business meaning. Include format notes if non-obvious.
entities[].relationships: Relationships to other entities. Empty array if none.
entities[].relationships[].entity_id: ID of the related entity (must match another entity's id in this catalog).
entities[].relationships[].description: What the relationship means in business terms, e.g. 'An order belongs to one user; a user can have many orders'.
entities[].constraints: Business or data integrity constraints not captured in fields or relationships. E.g. 'email must be unique', 'quantity must be >= 0', 'a published product must have at least one image'. Empty array if none.
entities[].test_fixture: A concrete example data object for this entity, used to seed the test database in Phase 4. Include all required fields with realistic values. For generated fields (password hashes, tokens, auto-increment IDs), use a realistic placeholder. Example: { "id": "usr-001", "email": "test@example.com", "role": "customer" }.
